title: Alert cooldown policy + Playbook Compiler for multi-region failover and graceful load-shed
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Problem statement: We continue to see noisy paging during regional transient failures where transient congestion, transient DNS flaps, or partial hardware degradation trigger duplicate pages across regionally-scoped alerts. This leads to on-call churn and delayed triage for real customer-impacting incidents. Concurrently, our manual runbook maintenance lags product changes (new routes, model variants, and capacity tiers), so runbooks are frequently out of date during failovers.

Goal: Deliver two coordinated capabilities: (1) an alert cooldown and hysteresis policy framework that reduces duplicate pages during transient degradations while preserving time-to-detect for true SLO breaches; and (2) a Playbook Compiler that synthesizes executable runbooks from canonical SLO definitions, routing policies, and recent incident transcripts so runbooks stay current across multi-region failover topologies and load-shedding permutations.

Scope:
- Design and implement a cooldown/hysteresis policy engine that operates upstream of paging: region-aware dedupe windows, error-budget-aware suppression, and severity escalation thresholds tied to aggregated cross-region signals.
- Implement circuit-breaker-aware alert enrichment so pages include current circuit state (open/half-open) and recommended mitigation steps.
- Build a Playbook Compiler prototype that:
  * Ingests SLO definitions, routing policy manifests, circuit-breaker configs, and the last 90 days of incident run data.
  * Produces a markdown + workflow JSON runbook that can be executed by the on-call app (step-by-step checks, safe failover toggles, and automated rollback hooks).
  * Highlights divergent manual steps that require human approval and surfaces replacement suggestions (e.g., toggle a route vs. scale pool).
- Safety constraints: Any automated load-shedding or failover action must be gated behind explicit opt-in toggles for Dedicated/Private customers and limited to canary scope during rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Pager volume reduction: Reduce duplicate pages from multi-region transient events by >= 55% in the pilot region during simulated flaps.
2) Mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) for true SLO breaches does not increase by more than 10%.
3) Playbook Compiler produces runnable runbooks for 90% of SLOs in the initial catalog (catalog = top 30 routes/models) and surfaces unknown steps as clearly labeled manual actions.
4) Playbooks are versioned and stored; a successful dry-run execution (simulation) must complete end-to-end without side effects in the staging environment.

Implementation plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks):
- Design cooldown policy primitives: region_dedupe_window, cross_region_aggregation_window, error_budget_tiering, and escalation_rules. Document policy DSL and examples in Confluence.
- Prototype alert processor that applies cooldown and outputs enriched paging payloads.

Phase 2 (3 weeks):
- Integrate policy processor with alerting pipeline (AlertRouter) and paging provider. Add circuit-breaker enrichment hooks.
- Create synthetic test harness that replays historical alert streams and measures page churn and MTTA impact.

Phase 3 (4 weeks):
- Implement Playbook Compiler: parsers for SLO YAML, routing manifests, and incident transcripts. Compiler emits markdown runbooks and a small workflow JSON for the on-call app.
- Wire compiler output to runbook storage and add UI preview in Console (read-only).

Phase 4 (2 weeks):
- Pilot in us-west-2 with two low-risk routes/models. Run chaos tests (DNS flaps, load surges) and measure metrics.
- Iterate on thresholds, add fallback to immediate page if escalation thresholds breached.

Rollout plan:
- Pilot: us-west-2 only, opt-in flag for teams. Run for 3 weeks and measure pager reduction and MTTA.
- Stage gating: expand to EMEA after meeting acceptance criteria and a post-pilot incident review.
- Enterprise customers: Ship as disabled by default for Private deployments; provide an operator guide to enable and tune.

Testing and validation:
- Replay historical incidents (last 18 months) through the synthetic harness. Validate no regression for major incidents (postmortems linked below).
- Run end-to-end dry-run for the Playbook Compiler in staging using 10 curated SLOs. Capture diffs vs existing runbooks.

Monitoring and metrics:
- New dashboard: multi-region-pager-churn, dedupe-window-hits, suppressed-pages-by-error_tier, MTTA, MTTI (time-to-incident-detection), and false-suppression-rate.
- Alerting: If suppressed-pages-by-error_tier > 5% for > 2 hours, auto-disable suppression and create P0 ticket.

Security and compliance:
- Playbook Compiler must not include any secrets. All runbook actions that require credentials should reference vault-safe handles and not embed keys.

Documentation and handover:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/Alert+Cooldown+and+Playbook+Compiler (draft).
- Operator guide: short checklist for enabling per-team tuning parameters.

Longer-term opportunities (out of scope for MVP):
- Use LLM-assisted summarization to suggest next-step text for runbook actions (requires security review).
- Tight feedback loop from executed runbook steps to refine automatic suggestions and thresholds.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We intentionally prefer suppression rules that are error-budget-aware rather than blanket cooldowns; this preserves responsiveness for high-priority customers.
- Playbook Compiler will initially target syntactic correctness and completeness; semantic accuracy of mitigation steps requires human validation and will be surfaced separately.
